Heard Sri. Liju M.P., the learned counsel for the petitioners, as well as Sri. N.B. Sunil Nath, the learned Government Pleader.

2. The petitioners are stated to be in joint possession and title of 4 cents of property comprised in Sy.No.1080/1 of Kadakampally Village, Thiruvananthapuram District, which was acquired for road widening.
An Award is stated to have been passed on 25.10.2022, as evidenced by Ext.P2.

The petitioners state that the Award was not served on them in time.
3.

In such circumstances, the 1st petitioner submitted Ext.P3 and the 2nd petitioner submitted Ext.P8 before the 1st respondent herein seeking for a reference, accompanied with an application for condonation of delay as evidenced by Exts.P6 and P10.
4.

The petitioners point out that in spite of submitting the afore applications, the 1st respondent has not taken into account the afore in accordance with the provisions of 2026:KER:29763 the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013.

sentences.text: Having considered the rival submissions as well as the connected records, I dispose of this writ petition, directing the 1st respondent herein to consider and pass orders on Exts.P3, P6, P8 and P10 applications filed by the petitioners as above, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
Needless to state, the petitioners shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity of being heard in the matter.
